# k0rdent_vpc_peerings (Data Source)

Every peering declared under one VPC.

**Only the ones this project created.** A counterpart's peering naming your VPC as its remote is that project's own resource and never appears here, so this cannot tell you whether a peering is half-open.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Only this project's peerings. The other side's peering back doesn't appear.
data "k0rdent_vpc_peerings" "training" {
  vpc = local.training_vpc
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `vpc` (String) Id of the local VPC whose peerings to read. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Optional

- `display_name_regex` (String) Return only the peerings whose `display_name` matches this regular expression, in the RE2 syntax Terraform's own `regex` function takes. The match isn't anchored, so `prod` finds `preprod-a`: write `^prod-` for a prefix. One with no `display_name` never matches. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Must be a regular expression in RE2 syntax.
- `project` (String) Project to read. Defaults to the provider's `project`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `state` (String) Return only the peerings whose `state` is this value. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["creating" "active" "deleting" "failed"].
- `tags` (Map of String) Return only the peerings carrying every one of these tags with exactly this value. Tags beyond these don't matter. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Every tag value must be set: a null value matches nothing.

### Read-Only

- `peerings` (Attributes List) The peerings, sorted by `id`, then `remote_vpc`. Stable under a reorder upstream but not under an insertion, so reach a peering with `for_each` rather than `peerings[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--peerings))

<a id="nestedatt--peerings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `peerings`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name, for display only.
- `id` (String) The peering's name.
- `remote_vpc` (String) Reference to the counterpart VPC.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this object.
- `state` (String) State of this side only. `active` does not mean traffic flows.
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined labels, as key-value pairs. Null when the object has none.
